items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XI, List of Answers on Terminology 9:1
items.html: The filling of HaVaYaH of AB is in the filling of Yudin, for wherever it shines, it brings the bottom Hey down from the Einayim, which came into being at the second Tzimtzum, and returns the AHP to their place. This is because AB of Atzilut receives from the corresponding discernment in AB of AK, where there was not yet any beginning of the second Tzimtzum, since the second Tzimtzum begins from the Tabur of AK downward, as is known; and therefore it is in the filling of Yudin, for the filling of Yudin indicates the first Tzimtzum, as is known. However, there are two discernments in this: AVI Ilain, whose way is in covered Hassadim, and their discernment from the Chazeh downward, called Yeshsut, whose way is in revealed Hassadim. And this is the whole difference between HaVaYaH of AB, which has four Yudin, and HaVaYaH of SAG, which has three Yudin. For in AB, which is AVI Ilain, there are four Mochin, namely HB, Hesed, and Gevura, and this is because Hesed and Gevura, which are the aspect of ZON of the Mochin, do not join openly to couple and to raise reflected light up to HB in order to bring the illumination of Hochma outward, since they are of the aspect of covered Hassadim, whose way is not to reveal the illumination of Hochma, in the secret of ‘for He delights in mercy,’ as is known. Therefore this HB is called by the name the hidden Daat, since they do not couple to expand in the illumination of Hochma. And they are therefore discerned as two distinct Mochin, and there are here four Mochin: HB HG, to which the four Yudin of the filling of HaVaYaH of AB allude.
